title: Asteroseismic Detection of a Massive Unseen Companion to the $δ$ Scuti Star TIC 160582982
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We present TIC 160582982, an eccentric $δ$ Scuti binary with a dynamically massive unseen companion. Six coherent high-frequency pressure modes used as pulsation clocks yield a phase-modulation orbit with $P_{\rm orb}=89.29\pm0.19$ d, $e=0.539^{+0.040}_{-0.037}$, and $a_1\sin i/c=145.6^{+3.7}_{-3.4}$ s, corresponding to $K_1=42.2^{+2.2}_{-1.8}$ km s$^{-1}$ and $f(M)=0.416^{+0.032}_{-0.028}\,M_\odot$. An independent frequency-modulation analysis of the two strongest modes gives a consistent orbital solution. Rotating MIST isochrones constrained by the atmospheric parameters and spectral energy distribution (SED) give $M_1=1.93\pm0.19\,M_\odot$ and $R_1=2.65\pm0.23\,R_\odot$. The mass function implies a formal edge-on minimum companion mass of approximately $1.80\,M_\odot$. Assuming a luminous main-sequence companion and including the non-eclipsing geometry gives $M_2=2.19^{+1.24}_{-0.34}\,M_\odot$ and $i=61.5^{+16.6}_{-19.6}$ deg. However, no clear evidence for the presence of a luminous counterpart is found, either photometrically or spectroscopically. This suggests the presence of a massive compact object, such as a neutron star or even a stellar-mass black hole, as the massive unseen binary companion. Future phase-resolved high-resolution spectroscopy will be crucial for obtaining an independent orbital constraint and clarifying the nature of the companion.

AI.tldr: TIC 160582982 is an eccentric δ Scuti binary whose pulsation-derived orbit reveals a massive unseen companion, likely a neutron star or stellar-mass black hole.
AI.motivation: The study aims to characterize an eccentric δ Scuti binary and determine the nature of its dynamically massive but non-luminous companion, which could be a compact object.
AI.method: Six coherent high-frequency pressure modes were used as pulsation clocks to derive a phase-modulation orbit; an independent frequency-modulation analysis of the two strongest modes cross-checked the solution. Rotating MIST isochrones constrained by atmospheric parameters and SED fitting provided stellar mass and radius.
AI.result: The orbit has P_orb=89.29±0.19 d, e=0.539, a1 sin i/c=145.6 s (K1=42.2 km/s), and f(M)=0.416 M_sun. MIST fitting gives M1=1.93±0.19 M_sun and R1=2.65±0.23 R_sun. The edge-on minimum companion mass is ~1.80 M_sun; assuming a luminous main-sequence companion yields M2=2.19 M_sun and i=61.5 deg. No photometric or spectroscopic evidence of a luminous counterpart was found.
AI.conclusion: The absence of a luminous companion suggests a massive compact object—a neutron star or stellar-mass black hole—as the unseen companion. Future phase-resolved high-resolution spectroscopy is needed to independently constrain the orbit and confirm the companion's nature.

title: Gaia neutron stars: demographics, birth rates, and connections to other neutron star populations
comment: 36 pages, 12 figures, including appendices. Submitted to PASP; comments are welcome
summary: Gaia DR3 revealed a new class of neutron stars (NSs) in au-scale orbits with solar-type companions. How these 'Gaia NSs' form remains unclear, and constraining their intrinsic population properties is a necessary step toward understanding their origin. However, the current sample of 27 Gaia NS candidates is strongly biased by Gaia's astrometric sensitivity. In this work, we carefully model the Gaia selection function and incorporate it into a hierarchical Bayesian framework to infer the \textit{intrinsic} demographics of the Gaia NS population. We find that the population favors a decreasing period distribution with power-law slope $α_P=-0.75 \pm 0.35$, a visible-star mass distribution peaked near $M_1\approx 0.85~{\rm M_\odot}$ ($σ_{M_1} \approx 0.2~{\rm M_\odot}$), an NS mass distribution peaked near $M_{\rm NS}\approx 1.3~{\rm M_\odot}$ with a tail towards higher masses, and an eccentricity distribution weighted toward moderate-to-large eccentricities. The intrinsic space density is $n\approx120~{\rm kpc^{-3}}$ within 2 kpc, implying that only $\sim3\%$ of the local Gaia NS population has been discovered so far. Our forecasts predict that Gaia DR4 will increase the sample to $\sim300$-650 NS candidates, including access to longer orbital periods that will provide direct tests of formation models. Finally, we place Gaia NSs in the context of the broader Galactic NS population by comparing their intrinsic birth rate, lifetime, and size to other classes of isolated and binary NSs. Only 0.01% - 1% of all NSs are born into au-scale orbits with solar-type companions, making the birth rate of Gaia NSs 10 - 100 times smaller than that of high-mass X-ray binaries and broadly comparable to symbiotic X-ray binaries.

AI.tldr: This work corrects Gaia's astrometric selection bias via hierarchical Bayesian inference to derive the intrinsic demographics of the 27 au-scale neutron stars with solar-type companions, finding a dense, largely undiscovered population that DR4 will expand substantially.
AI.motivation: Gaia DR3 uncovered a new class of neutron stars (NSs) in au-scale orbits with solar-type companions, but their formation is unclear and the current sample of 27 candidates is strongly biased by Gaia's astrometric sensitivity, preventing reliable inference of intrinsic population properties.
AI.method: The authors model the Gaia selection function and embed it within a hierarchical Bayesian framework to infer the intrinsic demographics of the Gaia NS population, then compare birth rate, lifetime, and size against other isolated and binary NS classes.
AI.result: The intrinsic population shows a decreasing period distribution (power-law slope alpha_P = -0.75 +/- 0.35), a visible-star mass distribution peaked near 0.85 Msun (sigma ~ 0.2 Msun), an NS mass distribution peaked near 1.3 Msun with a high-mass tail, and eccentricities weighted toward moderate-to-large values. The intrinsic space density is ~120 kpc^-3 within 2 kpc, implying only ~3% of the local population has been discovered. DR4 forecasts predict ~300-650 candidates with access to longer orbital periods.
AI.conclusion: Only 0.01%-1% of all NSs are born into au-scale orbits with solar-type companions, giving a Gaia NS birth rate 10-100 times smaller than high-mass X-ray binaries and broadly comparable to symbiotic X-ray binaries.

title: Eppur binaria non è esclusa: Pulsations in CZ Tuc appear to be tidally excited by its veiled companion
comment: 15 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Submitted to AAS Journals
summary: Long secondary periods (LSPs), observed in about one-third of pulsating red giants, remain unexplained despite decades of study, with binarity and non-radial oscillations as the leading competing hypotheses. If LSP variables are indeed interacting, eccentric binary systems consisting of a red giant and a substellar object, tidally excited oscillations (TEOs) would be expected to appear in a fraction of them. Therefore, detection of TEOs offers an independent test of the binary scenario that has not previously been applied to LSP stars. Using a combined, approximately 80-year light curve assembled from Digital Access to a Sky Century @ Harvard (DASCH), Hipparcos, and All Sky Automatic Survey (ASAS) photometry, we find that CZ Tucanae (CZ Tuc) exhibits a pulsation period of $55.4734\pm0.0074$ days along with its LSP of $443.62\pm0.12$ days, with a ratio of $7.9970\pm0.0024$ - consistent with a TEO. Theoretical models show the observed amplitude of the candidate TEO could be produced after adopting the estimated fundamental parameters of CZ Tuc. Our findings identify CZ Tuc as the first candidate LSP star with a TEO, providing independent evidence for binarity among at least a subset of these enigmatic variables.

AI.tldr: CZ Tucanae is identified as the first LSP star with a tidally excited oscillation, supporting the binary scenario for long secondary periods.
AI.motivation: Long secondary periods in pulsating red giants remain unexplained, with binarity and non-radial oscillations as competing hypotheses; detecting TEOs offers an independent test of the binary scenario that had not been applied to LSP stars.
AI.method: An ~80-year combined light curve was assembled from DASCH, Hipparcos, and ASAS photometry for CZ Tucanae, and the pulsation period, LSP, and their ratio were measured and compared with TEO expectations; theoretical models were used to check the candidate TEO amplitude against estimated fundamental parameters.
AI.result: CZ Tucanae shows a pulsation period of 55.4734 ± 0.0074 days and an LSP of 443.62 ± 0.12 days, giving a ratio of 7.9970 ± 0.0024, consistent with a TEO; models reproduce the observed candidate TEO amplitude.
AI.conclusion: CZ Tucanae is the first candidate LSP star with a TEO, providing independent evidence for binarity in at least a subset of LSP variables.

title: Theoretical RR Lyrae Instability Strip from MESA-RSP Pulsation models and updated BaSTI Evolutionary Tracks
comment: 21 pages, 12 figures, 9 tables, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: RR Lyraes (RRLs) are important tracers of old stellar populations and crucial distance indicators. To complement large variability surveys such as Gaia and Rubin-LSST, the topology of the RRL instability strip (IS) and their period-luminosity-metallicity (PLZ) and period-Wesenheit-metallicity (PWZ) relations need to be updated using state-of-the-art stellar evolution and pulsation models. We employ the updated set of BaSTI horizontal-branch (HB) evolutionary models, with finer sampling in effective temperature and metallicity, and compute the corresponding pulsation models using the mesa-rsp module building on the approach of Marconi et al. (2015). We compute a grid of linear non-adiabatic radial pulsation models with mesa-rsp, covering -2.2 <= [Fe/H] <= +0.06 dex. Seven convection configurations are explored including the recently empirically calibrated prescription for RRLs by Kovacs et al. (2024). Analytical IS boundaries are derived for RRab and RRc pulsators and transformed into several photometric systems (Gaia, OGLE, 2MASS, and LSST) and the Kiel diagram. The updated evolutionary models do not substantially change the pulsation predictions: RRab IS edges agree well with previous results, while the RRc red edge is slightly redder. The width of the IS decreases systematically with increasing alpha_MLT, and RRc is relatively more sensitive to the convection prescription than RRab. The PLZ and PWZ relations are also in good agreement with previous empirical and theoretical calibrations across the NIR bands; however, the convection prescription giving the closest match is wavelength dependent. The predicted IS boundaries and PLZ/PWZ relations exhibit a coupled dependence on pulsation mode, metallicity, and convective treatment, with no single prescription performing uniformly best across all observational planes.

AI.tldr: Updated BaSTI HB evolutionary models and mesa-rsp pulsation models for RR Lyrae confirm previous instability strip and PLZ/PWZ calibrations, with RRc more convection-sensitive than RRab and no single convection prescription optimal across all bands.
AI.motivation: RR Lyrae stars are key tracers of old stellar populations and distance indicators, but large variability surveys like Gaia and Rubin-LSST require updated instability strip topology and period-luminosity-metallicity (PLZ) and period-Wesenheit-metallicity (PWZ) relations based on modern stellar evolution and pulsation models.
AI.method: The authors use updated BaSTI horizontal-branch evolutionary models with finer sampling in effective temperature and metallicity, and compute a grid of linear non-adiabatic radial pulsation models with mesa-rsp following Marconi et al. (2015), covering -2.2 <= [Fe/H] <= +0.06 dex. Seven convection configurations, including the Kovacs et al. (2024) empirically calibrated prescription for RRLs, are explored. Analytical instability strip boundaries are derived for RRab and RRc and transformed into Gaia, OGLE, 2MASS, LSST photometric systems and the Kiel diagram.
AI.result: Updated evolutionary models do not substantially alter pulsation predictions: RRab IS edges agree well with previous results while the RRc red edge is slightly redder. The instability strip width decreases systematically with increasing alpha_MLT, and RRc is relatively more sensitive to the convection prescription than RRab. AI.conclusion: Predicted instability strip boundaries and PLZ/PWZ relations show a coupled dependence on pulsation mode, metallicity, and convective treatment, with no single convection prescription performing uniformly best across all observational planes.

title: Extreme Kerr Newman Black Holes: Differential Geometry, Symmetry, and the Golden Ratio
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures
summary: We investigate the geometry of extreme Kerr-Newman black holes and its role in selecting distinct black hole states. Motivated by Smarr's question of what physical information is encoded in event-horizon symmetries, we identify, besides the Smarr extreme family, a special family in which the mass, charge, angular momentum, and irreducible mass are constrained by a single irrational number. In the Christodoulou diagram, this family is selected by a discrete symmetry of appropriately scaled charge and angular-momentum variables. The local differential geometry of the event horizon provides an additional selection principle, which, up to the discrete symmetries (Q \rightarrow\pm Q) and (J \rightarrow\pm J), identifies a unique extreme Kerr-Newman black hole exhibiting the highest degree of local spherical symmetry compatible with the rotating Kerr-Newman geometry. Remarkably, for this distinct extreme configuration, all relevant physical and geometrical quantities, including the energy, electric charge, angular momentum, and irreducible mass, are solely related through the golden ratio. We also examine reversible and irreversible transformations and the associated extractable energy. Intrinsic horizon geometry can therefore constrain the macroscopic parameters and single out distinct extreme Kerr-Newman configurations.

AI.tldr: The local differential geometry of the event horizon selects a unique extreme Kerr-Newman black hole whose mass, charge, angular momentum, and irreducible mass are all tied to the golden ratio.
AI.motivation: Motivated by Smarr's question about what physical information is encoded in event-horizon symmetries, the authors ask whether horizon geometry can constrain macroscopic black hole parameters and select distinct extreme Kerr-Newman states.
AI.method: The authors analyze extreme Kerr-Newman black hole geometry, using the Christodoulou diagram and a discrete symmetry of appropriately scaled charge and angular-momentum variables. They then apply a local differential-geometric selection principle based on the degree of local spherical symmetry of the event horizon, modulo the discrete symmetries Q→±Q and J→±J. Reversible and irreversible transformations and extractable energy are also examined.
AI.result: Besides the Smarr extreme family, a special family is identified in which mass, charge, angular momentum, and irreducible mass are constrained by a single irrational number. The local horizon geometry selects, up to discrete symmetries, a unique extreme Kerr-Newman configuration with the highest degree of local spherical symmetry compatible with rotating Kerr-Newman geometry; for this state, energy, electric charge, angular momentum, and irreducible mass are all related solely through the golden ratio.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic event-horizon geometry can constrain macroscopic parameters and single out distinct extreme Kerr-Newman configurations, with the golden ratio governing the selected unique state.

title: Unresolved triples in the open cluster NGC 2437 (M 46) confirmed by the KMOS VVVX-GalCen Spectroscopic Survey
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Recent optical and near-IR photometric databases like Gaia data release 3 (DR3) and the VISTA Variables in the Vía Láctea eXtended (VVVX) ESO public survey allow the exploration of candidate unresolved multiple systems (binaries, triples, quadruples, etc.) in nearby clusters, that need spectroscopic confirmation. NGC 2437 (M 46) is a benchmark open cluster with well determined physical parameters. Its relative proximity (D=1.6 kpc) makes this cluster an ideal laboratory to measure the fractions of unresolved multiple systems. We aim here to identify unresolved triple and higher order systems that are reliable members of the open cluster NGC 2437, and provide the spectroscopic confirmation using radial velocities. We confirm that there is a sequence of unresolved binaries in NGC 2437, and report the discovery of a sequence of unresolved triple systems in this cluster. We corroborate membership for 13 binary systems and 8 triple systems using radial velocities measured by the ESO KMOS VVVX-GalCen spectroscopic survey. We further select stars with colors consistent with K-dwarfs, in order to have a controlled sample, comparable to the Solar neighborhood. We also find that the fraction of unresolved triples and quadruples is higher than that of the older open cluster Trumpler 19, studied using a similar setup, suggesting that these systems merge to form blue stragglers or get dissolved with time. We report the spectroscopic confirmation of 95% of the selected VVVX targets, thereby securing the presence of a sequence of unresolved triple systems in NGC 2437, located above the sequence of equal-mass binaries. The single stars constitute 60% of the mass of the cluster, while the rest of the mass (40%) is lodged in the unresolved multiple systems.

AI.tldr: Spectroscopic confirmation of 13 binary and 8 triple unresolved systems in the open cluster NGC 2437 (M 46), revealing a triple sequence above the equal-mass binary sequence and a higher triple/quadruple fraction than the older cluster Trumpler 19.
AI.motivation: Optical and near-IR databases (Gaia DR3, VVVX) enable exploration of candidate unresolved multiple systems in nearby clusters, but these candidates require spectroscopic confirmation. NGC 2437 (M 46) is a benchmark open cluster with well-determined physical parameters whose proximity (D = 1.6 kpc) makes it an ideal laboratory to measure the fractions of unresolved multiple systems.
AI.method: The authors identify candidate unresolved triple and higher-order systems that are reliable members of NGC 2437 and confirm them via radial velocities measured by the ESO KMOS VVVX-GalCen spectroscopic survey. They select stars with colors consistent with K-dwarfs to obtain a controlled sample comparable to the Solar neighborhood, and compare the resulting multiplicity fractions with those of the older open cluster Trumpler 19 studied with a similar setup.
AI.result: Membership is corroborated for 13 binary systems and 8 triple systems. A sequence of unresolved binaries and a newly discovered sequence of unresolved triple systems are confirmed in NGC 2437; the triple sequence lies above the sequence of equal-mass binaries. Spectroscopic confirmation was achieved for 95% of the selected VVVX targets. The fraction of unresolved triples and quadruples is higher than in the older cluster Trumpler 19.
AI.conclusion: NGC 2437 hosts a spectroscopically secured sequence of unresolved triple systems located above the equal-mass binary sequence. Single stars constitute 60% of the cluster mass, while the remaining 40% resides in unresolved multiple systems. The higher triple/quadruple fraction relative to the older Trumpler 19 suggests these systems merge to form blue stragglers or are dissolved over time.

title: Water enhances the formation of refractory sulfur in interstellar ices
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A). 5 figures, 1 table
summary: Sulfur is the tenth most abundant element in space, yet it is strongly depleted in the gas phase of dense interstellar regions, suggesting sequestration in dust grain components that are difficult to detect. We study whether UV irradiation and thermal processing of H2S-containing interstellar-ice analogues can produce refractory sulfur species, and whether water-dominated ice enhances their formation. We performed UV irradiation and warm-up experiments on H2S-containing ice analogues with and without water, and the resulting refractory residues were analysed ex situ. Refractory sulfur species, including the sulfur allotropes S6-S8, are formed during UV irradiation and thermal processing of H2S-containing interstellar-ice analogues. Water enhances the formation of these sulfur allotropes by two orders of magnitude. We propose a formation mechanism in which ionic intermediates stabilised by the water-ice matrix promote chain growth and cyclisation, yielding predominantly S8. The combined detection in our residues of sulfur allotropes and polythionic species, also reported in meteorites and samples returned from asteroids, supports their formation in pre-cometary ice mantles covering dust grains. Because these species can incorporate multiple sulfur atoms per molecule, they constitute an efficient solid-phase reservoir for the missing sulfur in dense cloud environments where young stars are born. Refractory sulfur can therefore serve as a tracer of water-ice environments in space.

AI.tldr: UV irradiation and thermal processing of H2S-containing interstellar-ice analogues produce refractory sulfur allotropes (S6–S8); a water-ice matrix boosts their formation by two orders of magnitude, offering a solid-phase reservoir explaining the "missing sulfur" in dense interstellar regions.
AI.motivation: Sulfur is the tenth most abundant element in space but is strongly depleted in the gas phase of dense interstellar regions, implying sequestration in dust grain components that are hard to detect. The paper addresses where this "missing sulfur" resides.
AI.method: UV irradiation and warm-up experiments on H2S-containing ice analogues, with and without water, followed by ex situ analysis of the resulting refractory residues.
AI.result: Refractory sulfur species, including sulfur allotropes S6–S8, form during UV irradiation and thermal processing. Water enhances allotrope formation by ~100×. A mechanism is proposed in which water-ice-stabilised ionic intermediates promote chain growth and cyclisation, yielding predominantly S8. Residues also contain polythionic species, matching detections in meteorites and returned asteroid samples.
AI.conclusion: These refractory sulfur species form in pre-cometary ice mantles on dust grains and, incorporating multiple sulfur atoms per molecule, act as an efficient solid-phase reservoir for the missing sulfur in dense star-forming clouds. Refractory sulfur can thus serve as a tracer of water-ice environments in space.

title: 1RXS J174320.1-042953: another polar with a red-shifted absorption component in emission line wings
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in Revista Mexicana de Astronomía y Astrofísica (RMxAA)
summary: We present the results of a spectroscopic and multi-band photometric study of the magnetic cataclysmic variable 1RXS J174320.1-042953. Multi-band photometry confirms a periodic modulation with an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb}=0.0864 \pm 0.0001$ days. Using the estimated secondary mass of $\sim0.15\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$ and, the X-ray-based white dwarf mass of $\sim0.75\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, we obtain values of $q\sim0.2$ and a system inclination of $47^\circ\pm10^\circ$. The optical spectra of 1RXS J174320.1-042953 are dominated by strong, complex, asymmetric, and highly variable single-peaked emission lines of the Balmer series, \ion{He}{i}, and \ion{He}{ii}, which are characteristic of polar-type magnetic cataclysmic variables. Doppler tomography reveals no evidence of a Keplerian accretion disc, supporting the classification of the system as a polar. The H$β$ and \ion{He}{ii} emission lines can be decomposed into at least two distinct components. The low-velocity components have semi-amplitudes of approximately 170 km s$^{-1}$ (H$β$) and 147 km s$^{-1}$ (\ion{He}{ii}), while the high-velocity components reach about 317 km s$^{-1}$ and 460 km s$^{-1}$, respectively. The low-velocity component is likely associated with the irradiated side of the secondary star facing the white dwarf and/or the vicinity of the L$_1$ point, whereas the high-velocity component is related to the accretion-stream structure. A redshifted absorption component in the emission-line wings is detected at orbital phases near $φ\approx 0.0$, reaching velocities up to $\sim1400$ km s$^{-1}$ and likely produced by accretion-stream material crossing the line of sight.

AI.tldr: Spectroscopic and multi-band photometric study confirms 1RXS J174320.1-042953 is a polar-type magnetic cataclysmic variable with no accretion disc, showing complex emission lines decomposed into low- and high-velocity components.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to characterize the poorly studied magnetic cataclysmic variable 1RXS J174320.1-042953, determining its orbital and physical parameters and understanding its accretion geometry through spectroscopy and photometry.
AI.method: Multi-band photometry measured the orbital period; spectroscopy characterized the emission lines. Doppler tomography was used to search for a Keplerian accretion disc. The H-beta and He II emission lines were decomposed into components, and a redshifted absorption feature was analyzed.
AI.result: Orbital period P_orb = 0.0864 +/- 0.0001 days; secondary mass ~0.15 M_sun, white dwarf mass ~0.75 M_sun, q ~0.2, inclination 47 +/- 10 degrees. Spectra show strong complex asymmetric variable single-peaked emission lines of Balmer series, He I, and He II. Doppler tomography reveals no Keplerian accretion disc. Low-velocity components have semi-amplitudes ~170 km/s (H-beta) and 147 km/s (He II); high-velocity components ~317 km/s and 460 km/s. A redshifted absorption component near phi ~ 0.0 reaches ~1400 km/s.
AI.conclusion: The absence of an accretion disc and the presence of polar-type emission lines confirm the system as a polar. The low-velocity emission component is attributed to the irradiated secondary star and/or L1 region, while the high-velocity component and redshifted absorption arise from accretion-stream material crossing the line of sight.

title: Which Milky Way Streams Make the Best Dark Matter Detectors?
comment: 29 pages, 18 figures;
summary: The abundance and properties of low-mass dark matter subhalos can be inferred by measuring the density and velocity structure of stellar streams, testing physical models of dark matter. Which streams make the most promising dark matter detectors, and which subhalos would they encounter? We use the semi-analytic model galacticus to simulate the Milky Way's dark subhalos, including tidal stripping under the influence of the galactic disk. Deriving stream initial conditions that best match present-day observations, we forecast subhalo encounters for 24 globular cluster streams around the Milky Way. Over their lifetimes, the 10 most perturbed streams are predicted to each experience $\approx 2$-$12$ significant subhalo encounters with velocity kicks $v_\mathrm{kick} > 0.1$ km s$^{-1}$. Jet, AAU, GD-1, and Palomar 5 lead the list, with Jet encountering twice the subhalos of any other stream. The subhalos that encounter streams have been tidally stripped to $1$-$20\%$ of their peak mass and are twice as compact as previous works have assumed. A spectroscopic survey of streams with sub-km s$^{-1}$ precision could reveal the influence of dark subhalos below the threshold of galaxy formation. Predicting the abundance and scatter of low-mass subhalos that reach the inner galaxy remains a dominant uncertainty in connecting stellar streams to models of dark matter.

AI.tldr: Using the semi-analytic model galacticus, the authors forecast subhalo encounters for 24 Milky Way globular cluster streams, identifying Jet, AAU, GD-1, and Palomar 5 as the most promising dark matter detectors and showing that encountering subhalos are more compact and heavily stripped than previously assumed.
AI.motivation: Low-mass dark matter subhalos can be probed via the density and velocity structure of stellar streams, but it is unclear which streams are the most promising dark matter detectors and which subhalos they would encounter. This work aims to identify optimal stream targets and characterize the subhalos that perturb them.

They derive stream initial conditions that best match present-day observations and forecast subhalo encounters for 24 globular cluster streams around the Milky Way.

title: Probing Accretion and Outflow in V1180 Cas through High-Resolution Optical Spectroscopy
comment: Accepted for publication in the Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy (JoAA), 17 pages with 5 figures
summary: We present an analysis of a high-resolution optical spectrum of V1180 Cas obtained with HIRES at the W. M. Keck Observatory during a bright photometric state of the source. The spectrum is dominated by strong emission lines, including H$α$, the Ca II infrared triplet, He I, and O I, along with numerous Fe I and Fe II transitions and several forbidden lines such as [O I] and [S II], indicating ongoing accretion and mass-loss activity. A weak Li I $λ$6708 absorption feature confirms the youth of the source. Using the Li I absorption and selected Fe I emission lines, we report for the first time a radial velocity of $-16 \pm 3$ km s$^{-1}$ for V1180 Cas. The H$α$ and H$β$ profiles exhibit asymmetric structures with blueshifted absorption components, suggesting outflowing material along the line of sight. The He I $λ$5876 line displays a narrow component likely associated with post-shock accretion regions and a broad, slightly blueshifted component probably arising from magnetospheric flows and/or inner disk winds. The [O I] $λ$6300 profile is decomposed into low- and high-velocity components, tracing a slow disk wind and a fast jet. Using the forbidden [O I] line, we estimate for the first time a disk inclination angle of $\approx50^\circ$. The derived mass accretion and jet mass-loss rates imply $\dot{M}_{jet}/\dot{M}_{acc} \sim 0.01$--$0.03$, at the lower end of, but consistent with, the range observed for Class II YSOs. Forbidden-line diagnostics indicate densities $\sim10^{3}$ and $10^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$ with temperatures of $\sim10^{4}$ K, supporting a multi-component outflow scenario. Overall, the results support a picture in which V1180 Cas is an actively accreting, moderately inclined system hosting a multi-component outflow.

AI.tldr: We present a Keck/HIRES high-resolution optical spectrum of V1180 Cas in a bright state. Strong emission lines (Hα, Ca II IRT, He I, O I, Fe I/II, [O I], [S II]) indicate ongoing accretion and mass loss; Li I λ6708 confirms youth. We report the first radial velocity of −16 ± 3 km/s, derive a disk inclination of ≈50° from [O I], and infer multi-component outflows with Ṁ_jet/Ṁ_acc ~ 0.01–0.03.
AI.motivation: V1180 Cas is a young stellar object, but its accretion and outflow properties, kinematics, and disk geometry are poorly constrained. This work aims to characterize its accretion and mass-loss activity, measure its radial velocity and disk inclination for the first time, and place its jet efficiency in the context of Class II YSOs.
AI.method: High-resolution optical spectroscopy of V1180 Cas with HIRES at Keck during a bright photometric state. Analysis of emission lines (Hα, Hβ, Ca II IRT, He I, O I, Fe I/II), forbidden lines ([O I], [S II]), and the Li I λ6708 absorption feature. Diagnostics include line-profile decomposition (blueshifted absorption, narrow/broad He I components, low- and high-velocity [O I]), forbidden-line density/temperature diagnostics, radial velocity from Li I absorption and selected Fe I lines, disk inclination from [O I], and mass accretion/jet mass-loss rate estimates.
AI.result: The spectrum is dominated by strong emission lines plus Fe I/Fe II and forbidden lines, showing active accretion and mass loss. A weak Li I λ6708 absorption confirms the source's youth. First radial velocity: −16 ± 3 km/s. Hα and Hβ show asymmetric profiles with blueshifted absorption, indicating line-of-sight outflow. He I λ5876 has a narrow component (post-shock accretion regions) and a broad, slightly blueshifted component (magnetospheric flows and/or inner disk winds). [O I] λ6300 decomposes into low- and high-velocity components (slow disk wind and fast jet). First disk inclination angle: ≈50°. Derived Ṁ_jet/Ṁ_acc ~ 0.01–0.03, at the lower end but consistent with Class II YSOs. Forbidden-line diagnostics give densities ~10^3 and 10^6 cm^-3 at ~10^4 K.
AI.conclusion: V1180 Cas is an actively accreting, moderately inclined (≈50°) young system hosting a multi-component outflow (slow disk wind plus fast jet), consistent with Class II YSO accretion/outflow behavior.

title: LIGHTS. Limitations of Far-Infrared Tracers for Galactic Cirrus Mitigation in the Era of Ultra-Deep Imaging
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. Fig.5 summarizes our modeling approach & Fig.6 shows the outcome of our Galactic Cirrus removal method
summary: Current and forthcoming deep optical imaging surveys are reaching surface brightness levels fainter than 30 mag/arcsec$^2$, where Galactic cirrus emission becomes a significant contaminant. This poses a major challenge for the study of extremely low-surface-brightness extragalactic structures. We investigate the relationship between far-infrared emission, as traced by the Herschel 250 $μ$m band, and optical surface brightness in the Sloan \textit{g}- and \textit{r}-bands. We find that, for Galactic cirrus with $μ_g\gtrsim$~27 mag/arcsec$^2$, a linear relation is consistent with the data, assuming optically thin dust, with optical cirrus emission amounting to $\sim$0.1\% of the far-infrared flux. Using Herschel far-infrared data to trace Galactic cirrus enables its identification over wide areas, but at the cost of significantly reducing spatial resolution. This limitation introduces source confusion and restricts the effective surface brightness depth that can be robustly probed in optical data. We show that, when cirrus emission is modeled using Herschel 250 $μ$m data, the limiting surface brightness is $μ_V\sim$~28 mag/arcsec$^2$, substantially shallower than the nominal depth of surveys such as LIGHTS or the 10-year coadd LSST ($μ_V\sim$~30.5 mag/arcsec$^2$). These results highlight a fundamental limitation in the use of currently available far-infrared data for cirrus mitigation in ultra-deep optical imaging, and emphasize the need for higher-resolution cirrus tracers to fully exploit the depth of upcoming surveys.

AI.tldr: Galactic cirrus contaminates ultra-deep optical surveys; using Herschel 250 μm to model it limits the usable surface brightness depth to μ_V~28 mag/arcsec², shallower than nominal depths of ~30.5 mag/arcsec² for LIGHTS and LSST coadds.
AI.motivation: Upcoming deep optical imaging surveys reach surface brightness fainter than 30 mag/arcsec², where Galactic cirrus becomes a dominant contaminant, challenging studies of extremely low-surface-brightness extragalactic structures. A method is needed to identify and mitigate cirrus, and to assess how much it limits usable survey depth.
AI.method: The authors compare far-infrared emission traced by the Herschel 250 μm band with optical surface brightness in Sloan g- and r-bands, testing whether a linear relation holds for optically thin dust at μ_g ≳ 27 mag/arcsec². They then model cirrus emission using Herschel 250 μm data and evaluate the resulting limiting surface brightness in optical imaging.
AI.result: For Galactic cirrus with μ_g ≳ 27 mag/arcsec², a linear relation is consistent with the data under the optically thin dust assumption, with optical cirrus emission amounting to ~0.1% of the far-infrared flux. Herschel data enable wide-area cirrus identification but at low spatial resolution, causing source confusion. When cirrus is modeled with Herschel 250 μm data, the limiting surface brightness is μ_V ~ 28 mag/arcsec², substantially shallower than the nominal ~30.5 mag/arcsec² of LIGHTS or the 10-year coadd LSST.
AI.conclusion: Currently available far-infrared data fundamentally limit cirrus mitigation in ultra-deep optical imaging, restricting the achievable surface brightness depth. Higher-resolution cirrus tracers are required to fully exploit the depth of upcoming surveys.

title: Structure of Convective-Reactive Zone in a Supernova Progenitor
summary: Convective-reactive events are phases of stellar evolution where turbulent mixing and nuclear burning directly compete, since their timescales become similar within convection zones. During these events the convection zone structure is shaped by a complex and dynamic interaction of convective transport and nuclear burning of individual chemical elements, with plasma streams connecting the entrainment regions with the burning layers. Here we analyse a 3D hydrodynamic simulation of an oxygen--neon shell merger in a massive pre-supernova star. We study the emergent structure using the Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) mean-field composition transport equation. We find that the merged convective zone develops a complex, turbulence-driven mixing structure of multiple nested convective-reactive shells, all contained within the single convection zone. Key controlling factors include not only the mean stratification and mixing, but also emergent collective behaviour of involved nuclear reactions for every chemical isotope. Almost all layers show a quasi-steady balance between burning and mixing. We categorise the various layers, and discuss/contrast with 1D stellar evolution code treatments, highlighting some implications.

AI.tldr: A 3D hydrodynamic simulation of an oxygen–neon shell merger in a massive pre-supernova star is analyzed via the RANS mean-field composition transport equation, revealing a single convection zone containing multiple nested convective-reactive shells.
AI.motivation: Convective-reactive events occur when turbulent mixing and nuclear burning timescales become comparable within convection zones, making the zone structure governed by a complex, dynamic coupling of convective transport and burning of individual elements. Understanding this emergent structure and how it departs from standard 1D treatments is the paper's aim.
AI.method: The authors analyze a 3D hydrodynamic simulation of an oxygen–neon shell merger in a massive pre-supernova star, studying the emergent structure using the Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) mean-field composition transport equation.
AI.result: The merged convective zone develops a complex, turbulence-driven mixing structure consisting of multiple nested convective-reactive shells within a single convection zone. Controlling factors include the mean stratification, mixing, and emergent collective behaviour of nuclear reactions for each isotope. Almost all layers exhibit a quasi-steady balance between burning and mixing; the layers are categorized accordingly.

title: The impact of relativistic AGN jets on realistic galaxy cluster environments
comment: Accepted in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Context. Low-power FRI-like radio jets dominate the AGN population, yet the main mechanism of heating the intracluster medium (ICM) and its efficiency remain a matter of debate. Aims. We investigate the impact of intermediate-power FRI-like relativistic jets on the inner region of realistic ICM, focusing on the role of weak shocks on heating and the environmental coupling in regulating energy deposition. Methods. We present six three-dimensional relativistic-hydrodynamic simulations of (1e44 - 1e45) erg/s FRI-like jets propagating through the central regions of realistic ICM environments extracted from cosmological GADGET-3 runs. Each simulation tracks 20 Myr of continuous jet activity with radiative cooling included. Results. Despite their intermediate power and mildly relativistic speed at injection, they decelerate rapidly to trans-sonic velocities (average Mach numbers ~ 2.3) and generate weak bow shocks that dominate the energy transfer. Approximately, 80% of the injected kinetic power is converted into internal energy of the ambient ICM, and bremsstrahlung cooling noticeably reduces the temperature of the shocked shells as they expand. Conclusions. Our results demonstrate that heating of the intergalactic and intracluster medium is highly efficient even in the case of weak shocks in FRI-like sources. This finding suggests low-power jets are a viable solution to the long-standing cooling-flow problem and likely regulate star formation across diverse galaxy cluster environments.

AI.tldr: Intermediate-power FRI-like relativistic jets are highly efficient at heating the intracluster medium via weak bow shocks, converting ~80% of injected kinetic power into internal energy of the ambient gas.
AI.motivation: Low-power FRI-like radio jets dominate the AGN population, yet the main mechanism by which they heat the intracluster medium (ICM) and the efficiency of that heating remain debated. This work aims to clarify the impact of intermediate-power FRI-like relativistic jets on the inner region of realistic ICM, focusing on the role of weak shocks in heating and on how environmental coupling regulates energy deposition.
AI.method: Six three-dimensional relativistic-hydrodynamic simulations of FRI-like jets with powers of 1e44-1e45 erg/s, propagating through the central regions of realistic ICM environments extracted from cosmological GADGET-3 runs. Each simulation tracks 20 Myr of continuous jet activity and includes radiative cooling.
AI.result: Despite their intermediate power and mildly relativistic injection speed, the jets decelerate rapidly to trans-sonic velocities (average Mach numbers ~2.3) and generate weak bow shocks that dominate energy transfer. Approximately 80% of the injected kinetic power is converted into internal energy of the ambient ICM, and bremsstrahlung cooling noticeably reduces the temperature of the expanding shocked shells.
AI.conclusion: Heating of the intergalactic and intracluster medium is highly efficient even for weak shocks in FRI-like sources. This suggests that low-power jets are a viable solution to the long-standing cooling-flow problem and likely regulate star formation across diverse galaxy cluster environments.

title: Towards solar many-line inversions
comment: PhD Thesis
summary: The Sun's atmosphere is significantly influenced by events that often measure only tens of kilometres in the horizontal direction. They happen in both quiet and active regions and are determined by magneto-hydro-dynamic processes. Their origins often lie in the lowest layers of the solar atmosphere. To improve the understanding of chromospheric and coronal heating, the solar dynamo and its activity cycle, or to improve the prediction of space weather events we must therefore enhance our understanding of such small-scale events. In this work I first describe the process of calibrating spectropolarimetric observations with very high spatial resolution and put together the building blocks for the mathematical proof the MOMFBD image reconstruction algorithm. In the second part I describe the FISS-SP prototype which is designed to fully exploit the resolution power of a 1.6m telescope. This instrument is built to provide suitable data for image reconstruction of spectropolarimetric data. The resulting data can resolve small-scale features down to the diffraction limit. The simultaneous interpretation of a few lines is still the norm for spatially highly resolved solar spectra. Theoretical works have shown that the simultaneous interpretation of multiple solar lines can greatly improve the robustness against noise. Using observations from FISS-SP I advance the theoretical idea into a practical technique. With this I can retrieve a coherent model of the local solar atmosphere, resolving structures down to a horizontal size of about 49~km. Finally, I use those new techniques to interpret an observation of a solar pore. In this last part I describe and analyse small-scale structures, which could not be spectropolarimetrically resolved before. Typical pore-boundary features - namely, dark striations with bright grains moving into the pore - are identified as convective features.

AI.tldr: This work advances high-resolution solar spectropolarimetry by calibrating observations, proving the MOMFBD reconstruction algorithm, developing the FISS-SP prototype for a 1.6m telescope, and applying multi-line inversion to resolve small-scale structures down to ~49 km, revealing pore-boundary features as convective.
AI.motivation: Small-scale solar atmospheric events (tens of km) drive chromospheric/coronal heating, the solar dynamo cycle, and space weather, but their origins lie in the lowest atmospheric layers. Understanding these requires spatially resolved spectropolarimetric data and robust interpretation methods, which are currently limited.
AI.method: The author calibrates high-spatial-resolution spectropolarimetric observations and assembles building blocks for a mathematical proof of the MOMFBD image reconstruction algorithm. A FISS-SP prototype is developed to exploit the resolution of a 1.6m telescope and provide suitable data for image reconstruction. Multi-line simultaneous interpretation is advanced from theory to a practical inversion technique to retrieve a coherent local atmospheric model.
AI.result: The FISS-SP data resolve small-scale features down to the diffraction limit, and multi-line inversion yields a coherent atmospheric model resolving structures down to ~49 km horizontally. Application to a solar pore identifies typical pore-boundary features—dark striations with bright grains moving inward—as convective features that were previously not spectropolarimetrically resolvable.
AI.conclusion: High-resolution spectropolarimetry combined with multi-line inversion enables resolving and interpreting previously inaccessible small-scale solar atmospheric structures, improving understanding relevant to chromospheric/coronal heating, the solar dynamo, and space weather prediction.

title: The star formation history of Orion is structured and episodic
comment: 4 pages, 9 figures, 5 pages appendix. Submitted to A&A Letters. Comments welcome
summary: The propagation of star formation throughout a molecular cloud complex can tell us much about its physical drivers and the importance of environmental versus intrinsic processes. We reconstruct the star formation history (SFH) of the Orion star-forming complex using the highest-resolution age map currently available. It comprises 47 co-spatial and co-moving groups identified by the SigMA clustering algorithm, with homogeneously derived ages and group memberships. We find four periods of increased star formation, separated by ~5 Myr each. The two periods of highest increase, at 6.4 and 11.3 Myr, can be statistically localized, together hold ca. 59% of all stars, and are robust against resampling and changes to the age fitting. The two older, smaller increases at 16.2 and 21.4 Myr can be identified in the age distribution, but cannot be shown to be robust at this point. The ~5 Myr spacing between the episodes of increased star formation is the same as found for the nearby Scorpius-Centaurus (Sco-Cen) star-forming region. We find no methodological bias that could produce the SFH structure. We identify spatio-temporally connected structures, including three cluster-chain candidates. We conclude that star formation in Orion seems to occur on the same timescales but with a different pattern than in Sco-Cen. The cause of the ~5 Myr separations remains a mystery, and its detection in two distinct star-forming regions needs further investigation.

AI.tldr: The Orion star-forming complex's history shows four bursts of star formation spaced ~5 Myr apart, a timescale also seen in Sco-Cen, though the cause of this spacing remains unexplained.
AI.motivation: Understanding how star formation propagates through a molecular cloud complex can reveal its physical drivers and clarify the relative importance of environmental versus intrinsic processes. The Orion complex is an ideal target given available high-resolution age data.
AI.method: The authors reconstruct the star formation history (SFH) of the Orion complex using the highest-resolution age map currently available, comprising 47 co-spatial, co-moving groups identified by the SigMA clustering algorithm with homogeneously derived ages and memberships. They test robustness via resampling and changes to the age fitting.
AI.result: Four periods of increased star formation are found, each separated by ~5 Myr. The two strongest peaks (at 6.4 and 11.3 Myr) are statistically localizable, hold ~59% of all stars, and are robust. The two older, smaller increases (at 16.2 and 21.4 Myr) are visible but not robustly confirmed. The ~5 Myr spacing matches that of Sco-Cen. No methodological bias producing the SFH structure was found, and three cluster-chain candidates were identified.
AI.conclusion: Star formation in Orion appears to proceed on the same timescale as in Sco-Cen but with a different spatial pattern. The origin of the ~5 Myr separation is unknown, and its detection in two distinct regions warrants further study.

title: Solarprop 2.0: Modern charge-sign dependent solar modulation for everyone
comment: 41 pages, 15 figures, comments welcome, associated source code available at https://github.com/henningrwth/solarprop2
summary: I present a greatly improved version of SOLARPROP, an open source framework for building models of charge-sign dependent solar modulation of cosmic rays in the heliosphere. The transport equation of charged particles is solved by converting it to a set of stochastic differential equations (SDEs). The code now includes the full set of SDEs in two spatial dimensions, allowing for magnetic fields with latitudinal components, and it has been generalized to accommodate models in three spatial dimensions. Due to code parallelization and optimization, a speedup of up to three orders of magnitude with respect to the original version is achieved. Python bindings have been added for ease of use. The code has been validated against the results of several model calculations found in the literature. While excellent agreement is found in many cases, important differences are observed for two model implementations. Possible root causes for the differences have been investigated.

AI.tldr: An improved, parallelized version of the open-source SOLARPROP framework for charge-sign dependent solar modulation modeling, now supporting 2D and 3D SDE-based transport with up to 1000x speedup and Python bindings.
AI.motivation: The original SOLARPROP framework, used for building models of charge-sign dependent solar modulation of cosmic rays in the heliosphere, was limited in dimensionality, performance, and usability, motivating a substantial upgrade.
AI.method: The charged-particle transport equation is converted into a set of stochastic differential equations (SDEs). The new version incorporates the full set of SDEs in two spatial dimensions (enabling magnetic fields with latitudinal components) and is generalized for three spatial dimensions. Code parallelization and optimization are applied, and Python bindings are added.
AI.result: A speedup of up to three orders of magnitude over the original version is achieved. Validation against several model calculations from the literature shows excellent agreement in many cases, though important differences appear for two model implementations, for which possible root causes were investigated.
AI.conclusion: The upgraded SOLARPROP offers a faster, more flexible, and easier-to-use tool for solar modulation modeling, with generally good literature agreement; remaining discrepancies in two cases warrant further investigation of their root causes.

title: Star Formation Mitosis: The Effects of Particle Splitting on the Star Formation Outcome
comment: 25 pages, 16 figures, 8 tables, submitted to OJAp
summary: Particle splitting can increase the dynamic range in Lagrangian astrophysical simulations by several orders of magnitude. However, such methods can introduce numerical noise that may affect the rate of convergence, particularly for collapse problems where fragmentation could be artificially suppressed or enhanced. Thus it is necessary to determine how these errors propagate to key quantities of interest, and to correct or mitigate them where possible. Using GIZMO's MFM-MHD method, we perform a set of $\approx 220$ simulations of a uniform-density turbulent gas sphere undergoing collapse, systematically varying the cloud mass and radius, feedback physics, initial resolution, the pace and cadence at which we split particles and the sink (accreting) or single-age stellar population (SSP; non-accreting) particle formation prescription. Crucially, we compare with control runs that start with uniformly-high resolution without splitting. While we find no evidence for artificial fragmentation caused by splitting particles, particle splitting runs have a smoother density field than their non-splitting counterparts. Due to this, particle splitting runs exhibit minor differences in the density and turbulence statistics. However, they form about the same total stellar mass as the control non-splitting runs, albeit with a slightly different mass spectrum. As a result, particle splitting runs have a different evolutionary history, compared to runs without particle splitting, especially when stellar feedback is present. Despite the changes seen in runs where we split particles, the numerical solution lies within the scatter inherently present in these chaotic systems, which we model by modifying the initial turbulent velocity field. Our results here argue that particle splitting generally ``works" for star formation applications, despite some systematic differences in the specifics.

AI.tldr: Particle splitting in GIZMO's MFM-MHD collapse simulations introduces systematic differences (smoother density field, altered evolution history) but no artificial fragmentation, and results stay within the intrinsic scatter of these chaotic systems.
AI.motivation: Particle splitting increases dynamic range by orders of magnitude in Lagrangian astrophysical simulations, but it can introduce numerical noise affecting convergence—particularly for collapse problems where fragmentation may be artificially suppressed or enhanced. The propagation of these errors to key quantities of interest must be characterized and mitigated.
AI.method: Using GIZMO's MFM-MHD method, ~220 simulations of a uniform-density turbulent gas sphere undergoing collapse were performed, systematically varying cloud mass and radius, feedback physics, initial resolution, particle-splitting pace/cadence, and sink (accreting) vs. single-age stellar population (SSP; non-accreting) formation prescriptions. Results were compared against control runs starting at uniformly high resolution without splitting. The inherent scatter in these chaotic systems was modeled by perturbing the initial turbulent velocity field.
AI.result: No evidence was found for artificial fragmentation caused by particle splitting. Splitting runs produce a smoother density field than non-splitting counterparts, leading to minor differences in density and turbulence statistics. They form roughly the same total stellar mass as controls but with a slightly different mass spectrum. Splitting runs thus follow a different evolutionary history, especially when stellar feedback is present.
AI.conclusion: Despite systematic differences in specifics, the numerical solution from particle splitting stays within the intrinsic scatter of these chaotic systems. Particle splitting generally "works" for star formation applications.

title: Delayed, Line-dependent Reorganization of Pore Oscillations Following a Compact C8.2 Flare Observed by Sunrise III/SUSI
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: Magnetic oscillations permeating the solar atmosphere can be altered by flares. This could be due to changes in the atmospheric magnetic waveguide, the thermodynamic stratification, or both. To investigate this, we examine oscillations in a magnetic pore crossed in part by the ribbon of a C8.2 flare, using observations from the Sunrise Ultraviolet Spectropolarimeter and Imager (SUSI) aboard Sunrise III. We track the core intensities of eight spectral lines between 327-329 nm and show that oscillatory power in the 4.2-7.0 mHz range, measured around 30 minutes after the flare peak, exceeds the pre-event value in all eight lines by factors of 1.60-8.71. Conversely, in the 7.0-11.5 mHz band, the post-event intensity power is lower - approximately 0.13-0.41 of the original power in seven of the observed lines. Line-center velocity measurements support the lower-frequency enhancement. This delayed, line-dependent shift toward the lower-frequency band is consistent with flare-induced changes in wave transmission, reflection, or resonant response, although thermodynamic and magnetic effects cannot yet be separated.

AI.tldr: A C8.2 flare crossing a magnetic pore produced a delayed, line-dependent redistribution of oscillation power toward lower frequencies in all eight observed UV spectral lines, consistent with flare-induced changes in the magnetic waveguide or thermodynamic stratification.
AI.motivation: Magnetic oscillations in the solar atmosphere can be modified by flares, potentially through changes in the atmospheric magnetic waveguide, the thermodynamic stratification, or both; the relative contribution of these mechanisms remains unclear and motivates this investigation.
AI.method: Using Sunrise III/SUSI observations, the authors tracked core intensities of eight spectral lines between 327-329 nm in a magnetic pore partly crossed by the ribbon of a C8.2 flare, comparing oscillatory power in the 4.2-7.0 mHz and 7.0-11.5 mHz bands before and ~30 minutes after the flare peak, complemented by line-center velocity measurements.
AI.result: In the 4.2-7.0 mHz band, post-flare power exceeded pre-event values in all eight lines by factors of 1.60-8.71. In the 7.0-11.5 mHz band, post-event power dropped to roughly 0.13-0.41 of the original value in seven lines. Velocity measurements corroborated the lower-frequency enhancement.
AI.conclusion: The delayed, line-dependent shift of oscillatory power toward lower frequencies is consistent with flare-induced changes in wave transmission, reflection, or resonant response, though thermodynamic and magnetic contributions cannot yet be disentangled.

title: The Impact of Simulation Resolution on Dwarf Galaxy Stellar Stream Populations in FIRE
comment: 18 pages, 10 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: Cosmological simulations allow us to study galaxy-progenitor stream populations, allowing comparisons with observations to constrain galaxy formation physics. Previous work found that present-day galaxy-progenitor streams in FIRE have larger pericenters than observed in the MW, which might indicate that they tidally disrupt at larger distances, where the Galactic tides are weaker, than in the MW. One possible explanation is that they tidally disrupt too quickly because of limited resolution. At lower resolution, low-mass dwarf galaxies can be puffier and more susceptible to disruption. We build and compare dwarf-galaxy stream catalogs in two FIRE-2 cosmological zoom-in simulations with identical initial conditions (m12i) but different particle mass resolution (7070 $M_\odot$ and 880 $M_\odot$). The higher-resolution run yields a larger dwarf galaxy stream population (22 streams versus 14) using the same cutoff of 100 star particles, primarily because it resolves lower-mass streams (down to $\sim10^{5}$ $M_\odot$). Both simulations form streams at galactocentric radii < 50 kpc, but the higher-resolution Triple Latte simulation produces more streams at these small radii. We find that dwarf galaxies in the higher-resolution simulation begin disrupting at smaller pericenters than in the lower-resolution simulation. By cross-matching stream candidates, we identify counterparts for $\sim$89$\%$ of the systems in the lower-resolution simulation. For matched systems that remain on similar orbits, the higher-resolution counterparts remain intact for longer. The orbital properties of streams in the higher-resolution simulation are broadly consistent with the MW dwarf-galaxy stream population, in contrast to the lower-resolution simulation.

AI.tldr: Comparing FIRE-2 zoom-in simulations of m12i at 7070 and 880 M_sun particle mass, higher resolution yields a larger and more MW-like dwarf-galaxy stream population because low-mass dwarfs disrupt at smaller pericenters.
AI.motivation: Prior work found that present-day galaxy-progenitor streams in FIRE have larger pericenters than observed Milky Way streams, suggesting they tidally disrupt too far out where Galactic tides are weak. A possible cause is insufficient numerical resolution: at low resolution, low-mass dwarf galaxies are puffier and thus artificially susceptible to early disruption.
AI.method: Build and compare dwarf-galaxy stream catalogs in two FIRE-2 cosmological zoom-in simulations (m12i) with identical initial conditions but different particle mass resolution (7070 M_sun vs 880 M_sun), using a 100 star-particle cutoff, and cross-match stream candidates between runs.
AI.result: The higher-resolution run produces 22 streams versus 14, mainly by resolving lower-mass streams down to ~10^5 M_sun. Both form streams at galactocentric radii <50 kpc, but the higher-resolution Triple Latte run yields more such inner streams. Dwarf galaxies in the higher-resolution run begin disrupting at smaller pericenters. Counterparts are identified for ~89% of lower-resolution systems; matched systems on similar orbits stay intact longer at higher resolution. Higher-resolution stream orbital properties broadly match the MW dwarf-galaxy stream population, unlike the lower-resolution run.
AI.conclusion: Numerical resolution strongly affects simulated dwarf-galaxy stream populations: higher resolution suppresses spurious early disruption, yielding more streams, smaller disruption pericenters, and orbital properties consistent with Milky Way observations, indicating resolution is a key systematic in using streams to constrain galaxy formation physics.

title: Ensemble pulsational characteristics of eclipsing binaries containing $β$ Cep stars observed by the TESS mission
comment: 18 pages and 10 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Massive pulsators in eclipsing binaries provide precise, model-independent stellar parameters that, combined with asteroseismic constraints, provide powerful probes of interior properties and angular-momentum transport in massive stars. This study investigates the pulsational characteristics and their impact on the structure and evolution of $β$ Cep pulsators in eclipsing binaries. We analyse an ensemble of 65 $β$ Cep stars in eclipsing binaries, identify rotationally split modes where possible, and statistically investigate the dependence of pulsational properties on binary orbital parameters. We derive their interior properties using MESA model grids and associated StORM pulsation frequencies, together with an asteroseismic routine that tracks stellar age and rotation across the $β$ Cep instability region. Interior rotation rates are derived for 14 systems that exhibit rotational mode splitting. While differential rotation is tentatively inferred for HD 112485, the other systems, except CZ Vel, are consistent with quasi-rigid rotation. The seismic and evolutionary properties of HD 112485 and EK Cru are derived through detailed forward asteroseismic modelling. HD 112485 is one of the least evolved $β$ Cep stars asteroseismically modelled to date, with a core hydrogen mass fraction $X_{c}= 0.501_{-0.013}^{+0.009}$. The two reproduced zonal modes in HD 112485 are the first radial-order dipole pressure mode and the second radial-order quadrupole gravity mode, while the zonal modes in EK Cru are the second-order quadrupole mixed mode and the third order dipole pressure mode. A multivariate regression shows a negative correlation of the pulsation amplitude with pulsation frequency, and no statistically significant relationship with the orbital period. In addition, no significant relationship is observed between the pulsation frequency and the orbital period in this sample.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes 65 β Cep pulsators in eclipsing binaries to probe massive-star interiors via asteroseismology, finding quasi-rigid rotation in most systems, deriving interior properties for 14 systems, and detailed models for HD 112485 and EK Cru.
AI.motivation: Massive pulsators in eclipsing binaries yield precise, model-independent stellar parameters that, combined with asteroseismic constraints, make them powerful probes of interior structure and angular-momentum transport in massive stars.
AI.method: The authors analyzed an ensemble of 65 β Cep stars in eclipsing binaries, identified rotationally split modes, and statistically tested the dependence of pulsational properties on binary orbital parameters. Interior properties were derived using MESA model grids with StORM pulsation frequencies and an asteroseismic routine tracking age and rotation across the β Cep instability region. Detailed forward asteroseismic modelling was applied to HD 112485 and EK Cru.
AI.result: Interior rotation rates were derived for 14 systems with rotational mode splitting; apart from tentative differential rotation in HD 112485 and an exception in CZ Vel, systems are consistent with quasi-rigid rotation. HD 112485 is among the least evolved β Cep stars modeled asteroseismically, with core hydrogen mass fraction Xc = 0.501_{-0.013}^{+0.009}; its two reproduced zonal modes are the first radial-order dipole pressure mode and second radial-order quadrupole gravity mode, while EK Cru's zonal modes are the second-order quadrupole mixed mode and third-order dipole pressure mode. A multivariate regression shows a negative correlation of pulsation amplitude with frequency, with no statistically significant relation to orbital period, and no significant relationship between pulsation frequency and orbital period.
AI.conclusion: β Cep pulsators in eclipsing binaries provide constraints on massive-star interiors and rotation, generally favoring quasi-rigid rotation. Pulsation amplitude decreases with frequency, while orbital period shows no statistically significant link to pulsational properties in this sample.

title: Do Submillimeter Galaxies Trace Megaparsec Large-scale Structures? -- An Overdensity Analysis of 449 Submillimeter Galaxies in COSMOS
comment: 27 pages of main text and 13 pages of appendix and references. 17 figures in main text and 2 in appendix. Resubmitted to ApJS after addressing referee's comments
summary: We present an environmental analysis and overdensity catalog for a large sample of submillimeter galaxies (SMGs) in the COSMOS field in order to understand whether SMGs are signposts of megaparsec-scale overdensity structures. We apply the Poisson Probability Method (PPM) protocluster finder to characterize the significance ($σ$) and overdensity value ($δ$) of any overdense structures surrounding specific 'beacon' galaxies. These beacons include 449 SMGs from A3COSMOS (including 168 with spectroscopic redshifts, 52 of which have CO or [CII] 158$μ$m line detections), as well as a control sample of over 5000 main-sequence star-forming galaxies (SFGs) selected from the 40-band photometric-redshift catalog in COSMOS2025. We successfully reproduce 15 known protoclusters and clusters in COSMOS (including Hyperion large-scale structure, CL J1001+0220 at z~2.5, and AzTEC-3 protocluster at z~5.3), and report 26 new PPM-based high-overdensity ($δ$ $\geq$ 5), high-significance ($σ$ $\geq$ 5), robust candidates. We measure an overdensity fraction of 11.5-71.2% (1.3-61.0%) in the CO/[CII] 52 SMG (full 449 SMG) sample with different criterion categories, confirming that SMGs are signposts of overdensities compared to the control SFG sample. We also notice that the fraction is lower than 100%, indicating that not all SMGs are associated with overdensities. We thus inspect the JWST morphology and argue that the triggering of starburst in SMGs must have non-environmental mechanisms, for instance, merger and violent disk instability. Finally, we further conduct a spatial distribution analysis, finding that the location of SMGs in overdensities has a redshift evolution, with SMGs being more concentrated in the inner regions of overdensities at higher redshift.

AI.tldr: This study builds an overdensity catalog for 449 COSMOS SMGs and a >5000 SFG control sample using the Poisson Probability Method, reproducing 15 known protoclusters/clusters and identifying 26 new high-overdensity candidates, and shows SMGs are (but not always) signposted by overdensities, with non-environmental triggering and redshift-dependent spatial concentration.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to test whether submillimeter galaxies (SMGs) are signposts of megaparsec-scale overdensity structures, i.e., whether their starbursts are environmentally driven, which requires a systematic environmental analysis and overdensity catalog for a large SMG sample with a proper control sample.
AI.method: The authors apply the Poisson Probability Method (PPM) protocluster finder to characterize the significance (σ) and overdensity (δ) of structures around 'beacon' galaxies. Beacons comprise 449 A3COSMOS SMGs (168 with spectroscopic redshifts, 52 with CO or [CII] 158μm detections) plus a control sample of >5000 main-sequence star-forming galaxies (SFGs) from the 40-band photometric-redshift COSMOS2025 catalog. They also inspect JWST morphologies and perform a spatial distribution analysis.

title: LACHESIS: Robust stellar parameters through Bayesian model averaging of isochrone grids
comment: Accepted in A&A. 12 pages, 7 figures, 1 page of appendix, abstract changed from accepted version due to character constraints
summary: Accurate stellar parameters underpin much of astrophysics, from exoplanetary systems to Galactic archaeology. For isolated field stars, masses and especially ages are usually inferred from stellar evolution models, yet these inferences depend on the chosen model grid, and the systematic differences between grids can rival the statistical uncertainties of any single pipeline. We present LACHESIS, a Python package that determines stellar masses, radii, and ages from photometry and spectroscopy while explicitly accounting for the systematic uncertainty from the choice of model grid. We interpolate five independent isochrone grids in [Fe/H], log age, and equivalent evolutionary phase conditioned on the data, sample each with nested sampling, and combine the per-grid posteriors by Bayesian model averaging, weighting each grid by its Bayesian evidence. This delivers homogeneous, well-characterized masses, radii, and ages for exoplanet hosts and stellar population studies.

title: Chemical complexity in feedback from supernova remnants: first detection of PO+ in IC443 and W44
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Supernova remnant (SNR) may shape the physical and chemical properties of star formation. By releasing refractory elements into the gas phase, they inject material of pre-biotic relevance into molecular clouds. Such elements may be inherited by planetary systems and become relevant for the emergence of life. We investigate the presence of P-bearing species in molecular clouds impacted by SNR-shocks. P is a crucial biological element, but its presence and reservoir in molecular clouds remain elusive. We present high-sensitivity 3 mm observations obtained with the IRAM 30m, toward the interaction sites between the SNRs W44 and IC443 and their associated molecular clouds. Focusing on PO+(2-1) and PN(2-1), we derive molecular column densities and abundances in local thermodynamic equilibrium. We investigate the correlation between P-bearing species and the shock tracer Silicon Monoxide (SiO). We detect, for the first time, PO+ toward SNRs, with abundances X(PO+)~8e-12-5e-11, but no significant PN emission. PO+ toward both SNRs is associated with strong SiO emission, showing similar linewidths but velocity offsets, suggesting that PO+ preferentially traces the most compressed and more strongly ionised layers of the shock. By comparing the derived abundances with those reported in literature, we suggest that the PO+ abundance mainly depends on a combination of shock strength and shocked medium density. Our results indicate that P-chemistry in SNR shocks is shifted toward an ion-dominated regime, likely driven by enhanced cosmic-ray ionisation rates. In this scenario, neutral species such as PN are efficiently destroyed, while ion-molecule reactions favour the production of PO+. This suggests that SNR shocks may play a role in processing P-bearing material and shaping gas-phase P chemistry in molecular clouds, with potential implications for the chemical inventory of star-forming environments.

AI.motivation: Supernova remnants may shape the physical and chemical properties of star formation by releasing refractory elements into the gas phase, injecting pre-biotic-relevant material into molecular clouds that could be inherited by planetary systems. Phosphorus is a crucial biological element, yet its presence and reservoir in molecular clouds remain elusive.

Focusing on PO+(2-1) and PN(2-1), the authors derived molecular column densities and abundances under local thermodynamic equilibrium and investigated correlations with the shock tracer SiO.
